title: Space traffic management as global infrastructure
bottleneck: Low Earth orbit is becoming critical infrastructure — communications, weather, navigation, defense — but it has no air-traffic-control equivalent: no global authority assigns orbital slots, no binding right-of-way rules, no real-time shared operational picture. The US is transitioning civil space traffic management to the Department of Commerce, the EU and others build parallel systems, and fragmentation risks incompatible regimes. Building a trusted, global, real-time coordination system across rival powers is as much a diplomatic problem as a technical one.
why_it_blocks: Every other debris bottleneck — removal, tracking, avoidance — assumes someone can authoritatively coordinate; without space traffic management, orbit remains an unmanaged commons heading for the Kessler outcome.
current_state: The US TraCSS system is rolling out; ESA's STM programs advance; UN COPUOS discusses long-term sustainability guidelines. No operational global STM authority exists.
